verdict.rationale: Weave ships official first-party SDKs in Python and TypeScript. The docs describe decorating or wrapping functions with `weave.op` in both languages, and the Weave SDK is named directly. The GitHub repo shows SDK primitives for tracing custom agent loops (`start_conversation`, `start_turn`) and one-line `weave.init()` integration with major agent SDKs. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of building against the SDKs, and a documented SDK versioning/deprecation policy (the only release policy covers W&B Server).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: When you decorate a function with `@weave.op()` (Python) or wrap it with `weave.op()` (TypeScript), Weave automatically captures its code, inputs, outputs, and execution metadata.
Skills covers both the [W\&B Models SDK] ... and the [Weave SDK] (traces, evaluations, scorers).
Custom agents — wrap your own loop with `start_conversation`, `start_turn`, `start_llm`, and `start_tool`.
Class-based Scorers: Python classes that inherit from weave.Scorer for more complex evaluations.
